raw_case_text: A 44-years-old man was seen in the clinic for recurrent (R) flank pain of 2-year duration. Ultrasound and subsequent CT scan performed 2 years ago showed a (R) suprarenal mass. He denied a history of hypertension, palpitations, or syncopal attacks. Serum cortisol, ACTH, metanephrine, and normetanephrine were normal at 201 nmol/L, 2.8 pmol/L (NR 1.6-13.90), 29 ng/L (NR < 90), and 92.0 ng/L (NR < 129), sequentially. Similarly, aldosterone and renin levels were normal with aldosterone/renin ratio of 3.6. Serum testosterone and dehydroepiandrosterone sulphate were also normal, at 5.94 nmol/L and 3.61 mumol/L successively. He was labeled as a nonfunctioning (R) adrenal mass. He later admitted to a strong history of childhood contact with animals including dogs. His elder brother was operated for multiple hydatid cysts in the abdomen. There were no urinary or other systemic symptoms. General examination including the blood pressure was normal apart from mild tenderness in the (R) renal angle. CT scan abdomen in July 2015 showed a large well-defined oval shaped heavily calcified cystic mass at the right adrenal gland, measuring 8.5 x 6.6 cm on transverse and AP diameter, respectively (Figures 1 and 2). MRI confirmed the CT finding. The mass depicts low T1 and heterogeneous high T2 signal intensity with internal stripes in T2 resembling water lily sign but showed no enhancement. It is surrounded with thin rim of dark T2 signal likely representing calcification (Figures 3 and 4). There was a mass effect on the upper pole of the right kidney and in some areas it appears inseparable from segment VI of the liver. The radiological features were consistent with hydatid cyst. IHA for hydatid was negative at 1 : 80. He was started on albendazole (400 mg twice daily) and praziquantel 600 mg weekly, for four weeks prior to surgery. In view of the persistent loin pain and the large cysts (>=5 cm diameter), he underwent (R) adrenalectomy through a right subcostal incision without spillage of the cyst content. The patient tolerated the procedure well with uneventful postoperative course. Macroscopic appearance showed well circumscribed cystic lesion measuring 10 x 8 x 4.5 cm (Figure 5) with focal multiloculated appearance. Histopathology revealed dense fibrous capsule with three layers showing a middle layer with characteristic lamination pattern and focal calcification. The cyst content is a lightly dense proteinaceous, with a jelly-like matrix material (Figures 6, 7, and 8). No scolices or hooks were seen and no associated granulomas or neoplasia. The histological features were consistent with hydatid cyst. He was finally discharged on albendazole 400 mg BD for another four weeks.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 44-year-old man presented with a 2-year history of recurrent right flank pain.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient was evaluated for recurrent right flank pain of 2 years' duration after an initial ultrasound and CT scan 2 years earlier had identified a right suprarenal mass.
subjective.past_medical_history: Strong history of childhood contact with animals including dogs; family history was positive for an elder brother who underwent surgery for multiple abdominal hydatid cysts.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for recurrent right flank pain; negative for hypertension, palpitations, syncope, urinary symptoms, or systemic complaints.

objective.physical_examination: General examination and blood pressure were normal; abdominal examination revealed mild tenderness in the right renal angle.
objective.routine_investigations: Endocrine workup confirmed a nonfunctioning adrenal mass: serum cortisol 201 nmol/L, ACTH 2.8 pmol/L (normal 1.6-13.90), metanephrine 29 ng/L (normal <90), normetanephrine 92.0 ng/L (normal <129), aldosterone/renin ratio 3.6, testosterone 5.94 nmol/L, and DHEAS 3.61 umol/L. Echinococcus indirect hemagglutination (IHA) serology was negative at 1:80.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominal CT (July 2015) and MRI demonstrated a well-defined 8.5 x 6.6 cm oval, heavily calcified cystic mass in the right adrenal gland compressing the upper pole of the right kidney and abutting hepatic segment VI, showing low T1 signal, heterogeneous high T2 signal with internal detached membrane stripes (water-lily sign), a dark T2 calcified rim, and no contrast enhancement. Following right adrenalectomy via a right subcostal incision, pathology of the 10 x 8 x 4.5 cm multiloculated cyst revealed a dense three-layered fibrous capsule with a characteristic acellular laminated middle layer, focal calcification, and proteinaceous jelly-like matrix without viable scolices or hooklets.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Primary isolated right adrenal hydatid cyst (10 x 8 x 4.5 cm), confirmed by MRI water-lily sign and histopathological demonstration of a three-layered cyst wall with a characteristic acellular laminated layer despite negative IHA serology (1:80). The patient received 4 weeks of preoperative oral albendazole (400 mg twice daily) and praziquantel (600 mg weekly), underwent intact open right adrenalectomy, and completed 4 weeks of postoperative albendazole (400 mg twice daily) with an uneventful recovery.
